name: has_task_size_guard
pattern: 8 discrete items|task size guard|split the task

name: mutex_avoids_second_acquire_call

name: mutex_has_2hr_staleness
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: the 2h threshold itself is defined once in skill-lock.mjs (pinned in acquiring-skill-lock.json) — the calling skill only needs to know it must echo the CLI's recovery line.

name: carry_over_scans_silent_pass
pattern: kind: operational|PREVIOUSLY MARKED DONE WITHOUT EVIDENCE|Silent-pass suspects

name: carry_over_display_needs_attention_section

name: carry_over_needs_attention_no_auto_carry
pattern: Do NOT auto-carry|not auto-carry|do not auto-carry

name: carryover_forbids_wildcard_source
pattern: do NOT widen to|not auto-carry.*inline capture|inline capture.*not auto-carry

name: prohibits_bash_redirect_for_state
pattern: never use echo, printf, or shell redirects
why: S016/P061: canonical home is CANONICAL_STARTUP_RULES in the startup CLI.

name: step4_has_red_step_forcing
pattern: First failing test|Red step.*step file|step file.*Red step

name: step4_has_adapted_8_80_rule
pattern: 1.4 hrs|1-4 hrs|4.8 hrs|4-8 hrs|1.2 days|1-2 days

name: quality_gate_has_red_step_check
pattern: First failing test.*Technical Notes|Technical Notes.*First failing test

name: step11_does_not_write_sprint_or_progress_from_memory
pattern: Use Write to create SPRINT.md and PROGRESS.md

name: data_decomposition_is_gated
pattern: Skip for features with no persistence concern|Data features \(gated\)

name: data_model_check_is_gated
pattern: skip entirely for non-data sprints|data features only

name: step_checklist_created
why: PLAN mode creates the 20-step task checklist so skipped steps are visible

name: task_list_never_authority
why: tasks are a progress mirror + recovery anchor, never evidence a step ran

name: recovery_uses_tasklist_anchor
why: compaction recovery anchors on the checklist, confirms against files

name: checklist_distinguishable_from_track_tasks
pattern: Step N:.*keeps the planning checklist distinguishable
why: v3.16.0: renamed from checklist_distinguishable_from_team_tasks — ship-execute track mode shares the task system for build tasks (main is the sole Task* owner across every dispatch shape); prefixes prevent cross-contamination. Pattern unchanged (still matches — the SKILL.md text it pins already read 'track mode' post-rebuild), vocabulary-only rename for consistency.

name: decomposition_deepdive_reads_models_think
why: v3.0.0 + S003: Steps 4-7 dispatch resolves the think tier via shipyard-data resolve-model and passes model: only when non-empty

name: decomposition_deepdive_dispatched
why: v3.0.0: Steps 4-7 run in one dispatched think-tier agent, not inline in the shell

name: decomposition_deepdive_structural_verification
pattern: structural verification|every returned step file path actually exists
why: v3.0.0: shell verifies returned step files exist and each feature has >=1 task before trusting the plan

name: decomposition_deepdive_has_inline_fallback
why: v3.0.0: on dispatch failure or invalid return, fall back to inline decomposition

name: decomposition_deepdive_no_askuser_in_agent
pattern: Never run AskUserQuestion inside the dispatched agent
why: v3.0.0: user gates stay shell-side; the deep-dive agent only analyzes and writes step files

name: capacity_decide_and_inform
pattern: Decide-and-inform when velocity data exists|say 'change' to adjust
why: v3.4.0: capacity with velocity data is stated in one line and proceeds; no accept/adjust ask

name: capacity_save_default_folds_into_approval
why: 4.4: capacity is never persisted from planning (velocity comes from archive-sprint), so there is no save-as-default question anywhere

name: planning_decisions_round_confidence_gated
why: v3.4.0: Steps 3.5-3.75 run the confidence gate; HIGH decide-and-inform, MEDIUM/LOW batch into one ask

name: planning_decisions_assumed_logging
why: v3.4.0: HIGH-tier decisions log ASSUMED entries surfaced in the Step 11 ASSUMPTIONS MADE list

name: rules_line_uses_confidence_gate
pattern: resolve the ambiguity before reaching for a prompt
why: v3.4.0: the blanket 'ambiguous -> ask' rule is replaced by the confidence gate + kill-list

name: stale_draft_options_labeled_by_content
pattern: Resume the draft with|Discard it and replan
why: v3.4.0: stale-draft resume options are labeled by feature content, not abstract keep/discard verbs

name: cancel_refuses_completed_sprint
why: S043: cancelling a completed sprint would bypass the archive review gate; the CLI refuses and the mode says so before touching features.

name: cancel_clears_tasks_via_cli
why: v3.6.0 wave 2: sprint-cancel's per-feature tasks: array reset is a dedicated CLI verb, not a hand-Edit.

name: cancel_uses_task_set_status_approved
why: v3.6.0 wave 2: sprint-cancel's task-frontmatter status reset routes through the task-state CLI.

name: uses_lock_acquire_planning
why: v3.7.0 wave 3 + CLI-call merge: the Session Mutex Check routes through the bundled shipyard-context sprint-planning call instead of hand-Read/Write or a second acquire call.

name: uses_lock_release
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: mutex cleanup routes through shipyard-data lock release instead of a hand Write.

name: no_hand_write_lock_file
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: skill-mutex lock files are CLI-owned — no skill body hand-Writes them anymore.

name: wave_count_never_capped
pattern: Never cap the number of WAVES

name: plan_score_check_in_validation
why: 4.19 (owner): the plan is scored for parallel work by the CLI; the per-wave caps of 6 and 12 are retired

name: plan_check_names_what_it_refuses
pattern: two steps of one wave that touch the same file
why: 4.19: the checklist names the problems the CLI refuses, so the planner fixes the plan and not the check

name: wave_is_as_wide_as_it_comes
pattern: A wave is as wide as it comes
why: 4.19 (owner): maximize parallel work; the only ceiling is execution.max_agents

name: steps_go_in_earliest_wave
pattern: Put every step in the earliest wave its `dependencies:` allow
why: 4.19: a step later than its dependencies require is refused by the CLI (late)

name: render_provenance_negation
why: v3.11.0 context-conflation fix: the render-before-ask rule must state the negative — Read results, subagent returns, dossier files, and SendMessage payloads are not 'shown to the user'. Anchors the same phrase check_render_before_ask requires. S016/P061: canonical text now lives in CANONICAL_STARTUP_RULES (bin/shipyard-context.mjs).

name: gates_user_flow_probe_at_plan_time
why: v3.17.0: a feature admitted to a sprint without a user-flow probe builds for hours before ship-execute Step 5.3 blocks on it.

name: probe_gate_is_cli_not_eyeball
why: v3.22.2: Check 24 is now a hard CLI gate (`shipyard-data story check-probes`) whose non-zero exit halts planning, not a model-eyeball checklist row that passed features through (sprint-034 S120/S121 slipped past the self-review and surfaced only at execute pre-flight).

name: deep_dive_draft_first_handoff
pattern: draft task specs.{0,260}before writing final step files
why: Deep-dive decomposition must not write final step files before the shell resolves required AskUserQuestion gates.

name: feature_tasks_updated_after_files_exist
pattern: story set-steps.{0,180}after every referenced step file exists
why: Feature task arrays are CLI-owned and must only point at existing step files owned by the feature.

name: sprint_deep_dive_sets_think_effort
why: Sprint planning deep-dive/analyst agents should use the configurable think-effort tier.

name: ship_sprint_uses_resolve_model
why: S003/P019: model+effort for dispatches come from `shipyard-data resolve-model <role>` (one deterministic answer), not prose re-derivation from config.md.

name: render_before_ask_short_reminder_present
why: S016/P061: the command keeps only the short reminder; the full doctrine is printed at startup (CANONICAL_STARTUP_RULES).

pattern: Use Write to create SPRINT.md and PROGRESS.md

name: no_hand_write_lock_file__extend-mode
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: skill-mutex lock files are CLI-owned — no skill body hand-Writes them anymore.

name: extend_router_reads_extend_mode_reference
why: P066: EXTEND procedure lives in extend-mode.md; the router must tell the model to read it.

name: mutex_avoids_second_acquire_call__plan-mode
pattern: Run `shipyard-data lock acquire planning --skill ship-sprint`|Run shipyard-data lock acquire planning --skill ship-sprint

name: no_hand_write_lock_file__plan-shared-steps
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: skill-mutex lock files are CLI-owned — no skill body hand-Writes them anymore.

name: plan_router_reads_plan_mode_and_shared_steps
why: P067 (S017 AC-4): PLAN procedure lives in plan-mode.md and the shared Steps 3-4 in plan-shared-steps.md; the PLAN router must tell the model to read both.

name: extend_router_reads_shared_steps
why: P067 (S017 AC-4): extend-mode.md E3 follows the shared Steps 3-4 'loaded above', so the EXTEND router must Read plan-shared-steps.md.

name: extend_mode_does_not_point_at_plan_mode
why: P066 rule kept by P067 (S017 AC-4): extend-mode.md reaches the shared steps through the router Read, never by pointing back at plan-mode.md.

name: plan_mode_keeps_determine_capacity_step
why: P067 (S017 AC-5): Step 1 heading stays stable inside plan-mode.md.

name: plan_mode_has_idea_backlog_gate_once
why: P067 (S017 AC-5): the CLI-backed Step 0.5 gate stays reachable on the plan path.

name: plan_shared_steps_has_rules
pattern: ## Rules\n\n- Capacity is a hard constraint
why: P067 (S017 AC-5): the Rules moved with the shared steps so both PLAN and EXTEND still load them.

name: shared_steps_exit_line_routes_plan_and_extend
pattern: \*\*Exit\.\*\* PLAN:[^\n]*go to Step 8\. EXTEND:[^\n]*go to Step E4\. Capacity: Step 1's in PLAN, E2's remaining in EXTEND\.
why: P067 (S017 AC-4): the shared steps end with ONE exit line so an EXTEND reader leaves for Step E4 (not the PLAN-only Step 8) and knows which capacity applies.

name: shared_steps_verification_defers_to_exit_line
pattern: If these hold, follow the \*\*Exit\*\* line at the end of these shared steps\.
why: P067 (S017 AC-4): the structural-verification step no longer sends an EXTEND reader to the PLAN-only checklist/Step 8.

name: extend_e3_ends_at_shared_exit_line
pattern: ### Step E3: Decompose New Features.*take the shared steps' \*\*Exit\*\* line: go to Step E4\.
why: P067 (S017 AC-4): E3 says where the shared steps stop and that the next step is E4.

name: shell_line_keeps_run_bare_rule
pattern: \*\*Shell\.\*\*[^\n]*Run commands bare from the project root\.
why: P067 (S017 AC-4): rule, not coaching: allowed-tools only matches Bash(shipyard-data:*) / Bash(shipyard-context:*), so cd-prefixed or absolute-path calls prompt for permission.

name: carry_over_scan_points_at_moved_ideas_paragraph
why: P070 (S018 AC-4): the paragraph moved out of ship-review/SKILL.md; the cross-skill pointer follows it.

name: plan_task_refs_not_labelled_agent_only
why: RF-06: shell reads these on inline fallback and the final step-file write, so they must not be labelled deep-dive-agent-only

name: plan_task_refs_no_agent_only_label
why: RF-06: stale label told the shell to skip references it needs

name: f011_capacity_is_cli_output
why: S011 AC-5/AC-8: capacity, fit and calibration come from one CLI; the planner never estimates and fits in prose

name: f011_fit_line_from_cli_at_selection
why: S011 AC-6/AC-8: the fit percentage is stated only with the CLI's calibration line beside it

name: f011_time_budget_flags
why: S011 AC-10/AC-11: optional time budget flags; points stay the default

name: f011_never_convert_hours_in_prose
pattern: never convert hours to points yourself
why: S011 AC-12: a time budget converts only through a measured (or labeled assumed) rate the CLI holds

name: f011_no_rate_falls_back_to_points
pattern: the CLI has fallen back to points
why: S011 AC-12: no rate means refuse and explain, never a guessed conversion

name: e004_risk_profile_lazy_capture
why: E004-S1: the risk profile is captured lazily at the first sprint that needs it, through the CLI

name: e004_risk_profile_cli_owned
why: E004-S1: harms are recorded only through the CLI (risk-profile.json is hook-denied for the model)

name: e004_floors_only_is_valid
why: E004-S1: unconfigured fails safe — baseline floors apply and skipping the capture is allowed

name: e005_design_check_is_a_planning_gate
pattern: shipyard-data design check <all in-scope story IDs>
why: E005-S3: UI steps need an approved, unchanged design — a CLI gate like check-probes

name: capacity_default_decide_and_inform
why: first-sprint capacity is stated, not asked

name: features_forced_choice_not_asked
pattern: Decide-and-inform when the choice is forced
why: one approved story that fits is not a question

name: no_save_default_question
why: capacity is never persisted from planning

name: step_files_never_run_full_suite
pattern: never tells its builder to run the project's full suite
why: 4.5: the wave boundary runs the suite once; per-builder full runs wasted minutes per step in a real sprint

name: plan_preclears_owner_gated_changes
why: 4.5: execute is unattended, so owner-reserved rule changes are answered at plan approval

name: plan_starts_from_reconciled_state
why: 4.6: planning never trips over state a previous cycle left stale

name: sprint_stops_its_helpers
pattern: Stop your helpers, then clean up the mutex
why: 4.9.1: planning helpers are stopped before the lock is released; the lock CLI refuses otherwise

name: planner_sizes_for_the_model
why: 4.10: step size routes the step to light/build/think, so S must mean straightforward

name: outside_targets_checked_at_planning
pattern: Everything a step needs outside the repository exists and is reachable
why: 4.13.4: a step was planned to update a published page the session's account did not have; found only at the end of the sprint

name: check_scenarios_gate_at_planning
why: 4.15.2: stories written before the rule are brought to it when they enter a sprint, never mid-execute

name: draft_ahead_mode_detected_from_context
why: 4.17 (owner): the next sprint can be drafted while the current one executes

name: draft_ahead_queue_next_only
why: 4.17: approving a sprint drafted ahead changes no story status and starts nothing

name: promote_next_documented
why: 4.17: a waiting sprint moves into current/ once it is free

name: chain_shortening_table
why: 4.19 (owner asked whether planning maximizes parallel work): the planner must question every link of the longest chain

name: step_declares_touches
why: 4.19: same-wave steps must not change the same file; the CLI can only check what the step declares

name: mode_from_widest_wave
pattern: From the widest wave, never from the step count
why: 4.19: sprint-012 built three independent one-step stories one after another because 1-3 steps meant solo

name: no_solo_by_step_count
why: 4.19: the retired rule must not come back

name: score_shown_to_owner
pattern: Show the score in the plan summary
why: 4.19: the owner sees how parallel the sprint is before approving it

name: probes_run_on_todays_code
why: 4.21: in sprint-011 four of five probes passed before any work; 'fails today' was one line in a checklist

name: probe_check_in_validation
why: 4.21: the planner's self-review names the CLI check

name: person_at_start_or_end
pattern: a person is never needed in the middle of a sprint
why: 4.0 (owner): involved early or late, never frequently during the build

name: plan_states_what_it_needs_from_person
pattern: Can you do these right when the sprint starts\?
why: 4.0 (owner): start items are settled at approval; a start item the owner cannot do leaves the sprint instead of parking halfway

name: decomposition_one_agent_per_story_group
pattern: one agent per group, all dispatched in one message
why: 4.0: a seven-story plan spent 13 of 47 minutes waiting for one agent to decompose independent stories; the plan score is the cross-group check

name: critic_one_per_story_group
pattern: One critic per story group, in one message
why: 4.0: one critic over a seven-story plan took 12 of 47 minutes; wave collisions are the CLI's answer, so critics can work per group

name: planning_decisions_one_card_each
why: 4.16 owner rule (one question per card, hook-enforced); the planner text still told it to batch up to four questions on one card

name: planning_decisions_not_batched
why: the hook refuses a card with more than one question inside any Shipyard command

name: critic_per_group_in_plan_mode
pattern: one critic per story group, all in one message
why: 4.0: the first live plan after the change still sent one critic (11 minutes) because the step the orchestrator reads said 'the critic agent'; the detail file alone was not enough

name: planner_sets_up_test_infra
why: 4.0 (owner: Shipyard should set up the test and build infrastructure at the best level): scoped and failed-only commands were left to the project and stayed empty, so every wave ran a 4 to 13 minute suite

name: extend_mode_rechecks_plan_and_releases_lock
why: 4.0: a live extension pushed a start-of-sprint person step into wave 2 (only the wave structure was checked) and left the planning lock held

name: extend_mode_sprint_check_is_plan_gate
why: 4.0: sprint check now also runs the plan's shape rules for the running sprint

name: planner_selects_from_nearest_release
pattern: the suggested selection comes from the nearest one that still has open work
why: 4.0.1 (owner: fix version concept)

name: planner_tells_the_tracker
pattern: Tell the tracker, when stories are linked to tickets\.
why: after 4.0.0 (owner: 'how about a scenario: jira story or bug ticket pull it discuss move to sprint'; 'will shipyard work with user session to update external ticket details along the way until up to completion')

name: planner_takes_from_the_top_in_order
pattern: The backlog's order is the selection order\.
why: after 4.0.0, LeSS (owner: 'fix this: What is not solid yet' — backlog order was RICE plus overrides; the review asked to 'accept')
